speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Intrepid.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, Houston. Are you copying the Noun 04? And we'll go recycle. It's plus 00476.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. Copy, Pete.

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid, Houston. You can close your fuel vent, now. The SHE [Supercritical Helium]'s holding.

speaker: Conrad
text: Roger; fuel vent closed.

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. How do you read? Over.

speaker: Gordon
text: Loud and clear, Jer.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger [Long pause.]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, Houston. Are you copying those torquing angles?

speaker: Carr
text: Affirmative, Pete. We got them.

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. Over.

speaker: Gordon
text: Houston, Yankee Clipper here.

speaker: Bean
text: Houston, did you copy the results of the AGS Cal?

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston, did you copy the results of the AGS CAL? [Pause while Carr finishes a brief engineering conversation with Dick Gordon]

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, this is Houston. Would you check you surge tank switch and the On detent? They were seeing a little funny in it.

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid, Houston. Go.

speaker: Gordon
text: It's in the On position.

speaker: Bean
text: Did you copy the results of the AGS Cal down there?

speaker: Conrad
text: Did you copy the results of the AGS CAL, down there?

speaker: Carr
text: That's affirmative, Al. Roger. Thank you, Dick.

speaker: Gordon
text: It looks okay. It's solid up here, Jerry.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger [Long pause.]

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. Over.

speaker: Gordon
text: Go ahead, Houston.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Clipper. We'd like to try something with your high gain antenna. Go to the Wide beamwidth and Auto. Over.

speaker: Gordon
text: Okay. I'm in Wide and Auto.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Dick [Long pause.]

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. Seems to be holding. Now try Medium beamwidth. Over.

speaker: Gordon
text: Okay. You got Medium.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Dick [Long pause.]

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston.

speaker: Gordon
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Carr
text: Okay, Dick. You're about a minute from LOS. We're satisfied with your surge tank pressures. You - we'll take a little - look in a little while at your S-band - next time you come around the horn. We'll be expecting to see you at 111:40 Over.

speaker: Public Affairs Officer
text: A bolter is an aircraft landing on a carrier that misses the arresting wire and has to go around again. Unofficial touchdown time of Intrepid, 110 hours, 32 minutes, 29 seconds. This was the time the blue touchdown light - lunar contact light - in the LM cabin came on and from first indications, the landing point is about 350 meters due West of where Surveyor is located in the East wall of the crater. 350 meters computes out to about 1,120 feet. We've had Loss Of Signal with Yankee Clipper as it went behind the Moon - around the corner. We'll continue to monitor Air To Ground for further communications with Intrepid.

speaker: Public Affairs Officer
text: This is Apollo Control. The crew of Intrepid are rather quiet at this time, doing some alignments of the Intrepid's inertial measuring unit, taking sitings on stars, other activities associated with powering down the LM, but we'll leave the circuit up in spite of the lack of conversation to catch any discussions that take place between Intrepid and the ground. Some 29 minutes until Yankee Clipper comes over the hill again. This is Apollo Control standing by on live air-ground.

speaker: Public Affairs Officer
text: This is Apollo Control. Lunar Module systems engineer reported to Flight Director, Cliff Charlesworth that at the time of touchdown, some 3.8 percent of descent propellants were still aboard at shutdown. Still standing by on air ground for resumption of communications between Intrepid and Mission Control. 22 minutes, 23 seconds until acquisition by Yankee Clipper.

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Houston; Intrepid.

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid; Houston. Go.

speaker: Conrad
text: I think I did something I'd bet I'd never do. I believe I shut that beauty off in the air before touchdown.

speaker: Carr
text: Shame on you! [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: No; I was on the gauges! That was the only way I could see where I was going. I saw that blue contact light, and shut that baby down and we zipped in from about six feet.

speaker: Bean
text: Boy, you can sure see the stars out of this AOT. I'm in detent 1 right now, looking at Sirius, and I can see the whole constellation [Canis Major].

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. Break. [Responding to Pete's comment about the landing] Pete, the Air Force guys here say that was a typical Navy landing.

speaker: Conrad
text: It's okay. As long as the hook was down and we didn't bolt, I'm happy.

speaker: Carr
text: That's affirm. You didn't get a bolter.

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid; Houston.

speaker: Bean
text: Go, Houston.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. We'd like to check out a couple of AGS addresses, when you get a chance. Would you read out address 233 and 464 for us, please?

speaker: Bean
text: Okay; there's 233. Plus 00250. 464 is plus 00500.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. Thank you, Al. [Pause] Those addresses are OK.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Houston; Intrepid.

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid; Houston. Go.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. We were marking on Pollux. And we entered one wrong number and did a Verb 32. Is there any way to wipe out that set of marks, now that we did a Verb 32?

speaker: Carr
text: Stand by, Pete. We'll confer with the experts, here.

speaker: Conrad
text: Forget it, Houston. I can do the program over again.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. They're asking for thirty more seconds [to consider the problem].

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay; we'll wait. [Pause] All we want to do is get outside, that's all. [Pause]

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid, Houston. The simplest thing to do is do the program over.

speaker: Conrad
text: We agree. Bye-bye.

speaker: Carr
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, Houston. You watching the DSKY?

speaker: Carr
text: Affirmative, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: And there are your torquing angles.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. They look great. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: And there's your Lat[itude], Long[itude], and altitude.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. Let us look at that for a second.

speaker: Bean
text: Looks like Dick did some good [landmark] tracking, with an altitude like that.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, Houston. It's even fun at one-sixth g inside of this spacecraft.

speaker: Carr
text: Don't break anything, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: No. As soon as we landed, we started handling the books like we do in the simulator at one g. We were throwing them off the table [laughing] and over near the circuit breakers and what have you.

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid, Houston. Recommend you accept Noun 89.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. That's done, and we're going to P00. [Long Pause] And if it's okay with you, we'll go ahead and do the second P57 right now. [Pause]

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Intrepid. Go.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid, Houston. Would you read us out AGS address 267?

speaker: Conrad
text: Coming at you. [Pause] Plus 10240.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. Thank you. [Pause] And Intrepid; Houston. We're just chasing a funny [an apparent peculiarity] in the AGS. We're convinced it's okay; and we're just trying to figure it all out.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. No sweat.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay; Houston. There are the torquing angles [from the second P57].

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Pete. We copy.

speaker: Conrad
text: Want us to torque?

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. Go ahead.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. What do you want to do with that one?

speaker: Carr
text: Let's look at it for just a minute, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid; Houston. Recommend you reject this Noun 89. Your first one was a little better.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Reject it is.

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid; Houston. If you go P00 and Data; we're ready to fire you up some new [state] vectors.

speaker: Conrad
text: Roger. Just a second.

speaker: Bean
text: [Noun] 047 is plus 37433. And [Noun] 053 is plus 05250.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. Stand by. [Pause] We got them, Al. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. It looks like you better tweak up your steerable [high-gain antenna] a little bit. It looks like we're beginning to lose a little signal.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, what do you recommend as the best possible angles? [Pause]

speaker: Carr
text: Standby, Al. We'll get them. [Pause] Intrepid; Houston. Try pitch plus 13, yaw minus 26.

speaker: Bean
text: The yaw'll be good, but the pitch isn't even close. Must be somewhere around 110.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. It's pitch 113. Sorry.

speaker: Bean
text: My fault. That's where we are now, Houston.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, Houston. You got P00 and Data.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Pete. [Pause] Intrepid; Houston. I've got the octal data for your P22 work-around procedure.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. We are ready to copy.

speaker: Carr
text: Okay. Your first one is 04645 Enter. And 35070 Enter.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. 04645 Enter and 35070 Enter?

speaker: Carr
text: That's affirmative, Pete. And I've got a DAP [Digital Autopilot] load update for LM weight for you.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. Your new LM weight is 10802 [lbs for the Ascent Stage].

speaker: Conrad
text: 10802. Roger. [Pause] And, Houston, are we Stay yet? [Pause]

speaker: Carr
text: Affirmative; stay for T3.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. We'll go ahead on [that is, continue] Surface [Checklist page] 9 and start our stay partial power down.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: And do you have a P22 Acq[uisition] time?

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Pete. It's on your lunar surface Pad. Stand by and I'll read it out to you again.

speaker: Bean
text: We got it.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Responding to Carr] Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Carr
text: Intrepid; Houston. We have an update on the P22 Acq time for you. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Go.

speaker: Carr
text: Okay; figure on 112:24:30.

speaker: Carr
text: Affirmative. [Long Pause] Intrepid; Houston. The computer's yours.

speaker: Conrad
text: Roger.

speaker: Carr
text: You have a new RLS [Reference Landing Site] and state vector.

speaker: Conrad
text: Thank you.

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. How do you read?

speaker: Gordon
text: Hello, Houston; Yankee Clipper here.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Clipper. Reading you weak but clear.

speaker: Carr
text: Clipper, if you'll give us P00 and Accept; we'll start your update. [Long pause.]

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston.

speaker: Gordon
text: Hello, Houston; Yankee Clipper here. [Long pause.]

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston.

speaker: Gordon
text: Hello, Houston; Yankee Clipper. Loud and clear.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Dick. You in P00 and Accept and ready for an uplink?

speaker: Gordon
text: That's affirmative.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. It's on its way.[Long pause.]

speaker: Carr
text: Clipper, Houston. I have a Rev 16 map update and a landmark tracking PAD, if you're ready to copy.

speaker: Gordon
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger, Dick. P22 landmark tracking PAD follows: T-1 is 112:20:00; T-2 is 112:25:11; the landmark is number 193; and it's South 06. Over.

speaker: Gordon
text: Roger. Landmark 193, T-1 is 112:20:00; T-2, 112:25:11; 6 miles South.

speaker: Carr
text: Affirmative.

speaker: Gordon
text: Okay. I'll see if I can plot it in the same place I did last time.

speaker: Carr
text: Roger. You got something new to look at down there, too.

speaker: Gordon
text: Let's - let's save them for the next Rev. [Long pause.]

speaker: Carr
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. The CMC is yours.

speaker: Gordon
text: Roger, Jerry. Thank you. How are things going on the surface?

speaker: Carr
text: They're doing great, Dick.

speaker: Gordon
text: [Garble] the same [garble].

speaker: Carr
text: Clipper, Houston. Give us Narrow beamwidth.

speaker: Gordon
text: Okay.

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid, Houston.

speaker: Conrad
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Gibson
text: Well done, Intrepid. You got a bunch of happy geologists in the back room waiting to go. Say, we're standing by with a LM consumables update and also standing by for your description [of the view out the window].

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. We were just working on that and I'm very close to where I want to be, but I'm trying to pin it down exactly.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Conrad
text: I guess, Houston, for planning purposes, we landed very close to the Head of the Snowman. [Mentally orienting the map with west ahead of them] I'm guessing exactly on the same [north-south] line as Selected Site 3 [which is at D.4,14.0], but a little bit further left [south]. Let me give you some coordinates here. This is my first offhand cut at it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Say, Houston; Intrepid.

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid; Houston. Go ahead.

speaker: Conrad
text: We're having a little trouble judging distance. How long is my [LM] shadow?

speaker: Gibson
text: [Possibly reading a chart] Intrepid, your shadow length on a level surface is 250 feet. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [Incredulous] You've got to be kidding me! [Long Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid, Houston. We could shorten that a bit to 230. Which way do you think you are?

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Well, if my shadow's 230 feet long, we're really misjudging distances [which they are].

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. Are you short or long?

speaker: Conrad
text: Well, I'd say that my shadow was much shorter than that.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. [Pause]

speaker: Gordon
text: Houston, Yankee Clipper.

speaker: Gibson
text: Clipper, Houston. Go ahead.

speaker: Gordon
text: Is - Is Intrepid going to do a P22?

speaker: Gibson
text: That's affirmative.

speaker: Conrad
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Gibson
text: A reminder: prior to your P22, I'd like you to execute Verb 41, Noun 72.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Going Verb 41, Noun 72. [Long Pause] What Verb 41, Noun 72 do you want me to do anyhow? I got it [the radar] pointing 270, 180.

speaker: Gibson
text: Stand by, Pete.

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid; Houston. The step you carried out on Surface 9 going to 270/180 is good.

speaker: Conrad
text: Understand.

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid; Houston.

speaker: Conrad
text: Go.

speaker: Gibson
text: We'll shorten that shadow length up for you a bit. If we assume a 3-1/2-degree slope all the way [up to the west], then you'll come up with a 150-foot shadow.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Then I'm judging about right. How wide a diameter is the Head of the Snowman? [Long Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid, Houston. Diameter of the Head Crater from one inside rim to the other inside rim is around 400 to 500 feet.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Right on the Head of the Snowman, to the left [south], let's use map 7-6 at coordinates M.5 and make it 10.5. I think that's a very sharp, blocky rim crater. Do you agree?

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid; Houston. The coordinates which you gave us, are those the coordinates of the crater or the coordinates of your present location? And, also, repeat your question related to the blocky rim.

speaker: Conrad
text: Well, I want to know if that crater that I gave you... That's not where I am. I think I have that crater in sight. And it's a very blocky rim crater, and I want to know if the crater that I gave you the coordinates of is a very blocky rim crater. I think I'm sitting right next to the head of the Snowman on the right-hand side at coordinates S... Wait one. Yeah, S.8 and 13.3. I think that's where I landed.

speaker: Gibson
text: Copy S.8 and 13.3. The coordinates you gave us of the crater are right next to Bench Crater. Do you confirm? Bench Crater being at L.5 rather than M.5.

speaker: Conrad
text: I don't know. Yeah; wait a minute. I got to get on this P22. Hold the phone.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, Houston. We're standing by to track [the CSM].

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Intrepid. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [Still examining the map] Yeah; it's Bench Crater. That's the one I'm referring to. And I think I landed at Head Crater, almost... Just a little bit past one of the traverses that you got laid out there.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Intrepid. And we're trying to decide here whether your present position is really R.2 rather than S.8. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah, you're right. R.2. I'm sorry. I'm reading it backwards. R.2.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. Thank you, Pete.

speaker: Bean
text: Houston, we're eating right now. We'll give a description here in another 15 minutes or so.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Intrepid. And we're standing by with a consumables update. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: I'm getting acquisition P22. Looks good.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Gordon
text: Houston, tell him I show him locked on.[Long pause.]

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Clipper.

speaker: Public Affairs Officer
text: This new estimate of LM location would put it about 750 to 800 feet from the Surveyor.

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Houston. Intrepid has a visual on Yankee Clipper.[Long pause.]

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Houston. Relay to Yankee Clipper I've got him visually.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Intrepid. Will do.

speaker: Gibson
text: Clipper, Houston.

speaker: Gordon
text: [Garbled]

speaker: Gibson
text: Clipper, for your info, Intrepid has a visual on you.

speaker: Gibson
text: Thank you.

speaker: Gordon
text: [Faint] Thank you.

speaker: Public Affairs Officer
text: This is Apollo Control at 112 hours, 30 minutes. The Change Of Shift news conference is about to begun at MSC News Center...

speaker: Gordon
text: Hello, Houston; Yankee Clipper.

speaker: Gibson
text: Clipper, Houston. Go ahead.

speaker: Gordon
text: Okay. Do you have all the data?

speaker: Gibson
text: Affirmative, Clipper. We have it.

speaker: Gordon
text: Okay. The next time, I want to see you put that Intrepid right in the middle of the sextant.

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston, Intrepid's ready to copy the consumables update.

speaker: Gibson
text: [To Dick] Roger, Clipper. [Responding to Pete] Intrepid, consumables update for GET [1]11 plus 50: RCS A, 80 [percent remaining]; B, 75: O2 descent, 87.6 and 97.4 [percent remaining]; H2O, 78.7, 99.2 [percent remaining]; amp hours [remaining], 1243.3, 572.3.

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston, Intrepid's ready to copy the consumables update.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Clipper.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, I got it all, except the only thing that wasn't clear was the time.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. That was for 111 plus 50 plus 00.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Got it. Thank you.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Are you ready for Verb 74?

speaker: Gibson
text: Stand by on that, Pete. We'll be right back with you.

speaker: Gibson
text: Okay, Intrepid. We're ready; Verb 74.

speaker: Conrad
text: Say, Houston. From your data, where do you think we landed?

speaker: Gibson
text: Stand by on that, Pete. [Changing the subject] We have a good E-MOD dump.

speaker: Conrad
text: I think it's just a matter of... [Hearing Gibson] Okay. I think it's just a matter of a few hundred feet one way or another. I flew right by the side of the [Surveyor] crater and ground her to a halt and parked it, but that's about my best guess right now where we are.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. We'll be massaging the data and be getting back to you on that. We have the data on the E-MOD. [Long Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid, Houston. On your previous question on Bench Crater, from our maps here, we can't tell whether that has a blocky rim.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Well, you can take the Sun line for a reference; [and] that crater's about 5 degrees off to the left of the Sun line of my shadow. And it is a very blocky rim. Big blocks. Depending on how far away it is, there's some blocks over there that may be 8 feet.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. Copy. You're looking at the crater which is 5 degrees south of the Sun line?

speaker: Conrad
text: Yes. Five degrees left of the shadow.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Soon as we get done eating here, we'll get with it. We're pretty hungry.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Intrepid. You deserve it. [Pause]

speaker: Gordon
text: This is Yankee Clipper. No, they don't. Tell them to get to work.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Clipper.

speaker: Gordon
text: They're down there having all the fun, and you're doing all the work.

speaker: Gibson
text: They'll get with it soon, Clipper.

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid, Houston.

speaker: Conrad
text: Go.

speaker: Gibson
text: Help us get a better visual pin-down of where you are. Are you able to locate a 50-foot block, approximately 100 foot [sic; means feet] right in front of you; [possibly correcting himself] or an 8- to 10-foot block about 50 feet in front of you? And that will be at R.5/13.1 . [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Well, I can't say that there is anything like that. There is one great big block that looks to me like it's 1500 or 2000 feet in front of us that meets that description. It's a really big fellow sitting out there.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Intrepid.

speaker: Conrad
text: However, what fools you, Houston... Let me say this: there's another large crater [Head Crater] right smack in front of us, but it's not obvious to us. There is no shadow length [that is, the shadow in the bottom of Head is hidden from them]. [The] Sun angle is so low that we're sitting here where we don't see any shadows; and, unless we look very carefully, it's not obvious to us that there is a big crater out there. Now, I kind of think that that may be the Head of the Snowman that's sitting out further past me. I'm not sure that I'm not sitting right smack on the other side [meaning the west side] of the Surveyor crater, just a little bit past it. I think really the best thing for us to do is to get out and look around. The sooner we do that, the quicker we'll figure out where we are.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Intrepid. We concur with that, and we're also standing by for your LM description. We have your lift-off times for Rev 16 through 19. When you're ready to copy. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Go ahead, Houston.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. Readback correct.

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston, this is Intrepid. Al's finishing off eating and, while he does that, I've been sitting here scanning with the monocular. And the first thing I should give you, according to the checklist here [is that], as you already know, we flew right by the side of the Snowman [meaning Surveyor Crater], and landed right past him some little bit. And our yaw angle is 10 degrees [clockwise], and my general impression is that we're in country where I see mostly angular rocks. [There are] very few rocks at hand that are rounded. Everything is angular. Now, I'll let Al talk about the close-up stuff [later]. Out on the horizon...

speaker: Conrad
text: ...horizon. [Stops to answer] Go.

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid, we'd like to get to Yankee Clipper before LOS, and we'll be right back with you.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. [Long pause.]

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid, Houston. Go ahead with your description of the horizon, and we'll be breaking in to you as soon as we can get back with Yankee Clipper. We've lost Comm temporarily.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. There are... The blocky rim crater that I previously mentioned... When I look through the monocular, everything has a pure white look; these big blocky boulders look pure white. Now, some of them are really big; and, when I say big, I'm talking 8, 10, maybe 20 feet. Some on the horizon [pause] got to be 20 feet across. [Long Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Intrepid, Houston. Your Comm is breaking up slightly.

speaker: Bean
text: We were laughing about that ourselves. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [Comm improves] Okay, Houston. I'm back on the air again. And just a general comment about all these blocks in the surrounding terrain: at first glance out of the spacecraft, I can distinguish absolutely no color difference in anything. About the only difference is looking cross-Sun [north or south] versus down-Sun [west, directly away from the Sun]. I'm sure that some of these rocks have different colors and different textures; but, from here, viewing from the spacecraft, they don't appear that way. Looking at all the materials on the horizon and the blocks on the horizon, they all appear to be of the same material, and they all appear to be pure white. Now, we've got a pretty low Sun angle and I'm looking at them at a low angle [so that they reflect a great deal of light back toward the spacecraft], so they [may] have varying other colors; but in this monocular, they all appear white. They are all very blocky. As I said, the size goes all the way up to, I'm guessing, 20 feet. A couple of big ones on the horizon [appear to be that size].

Also, we ought to press on here fairly quickly, as we are getting a little bit behind our timeline.

speaker: Bean

I'll give you a good description here; and we're going to get ready; and when we get out, we'll take the TV and show you the craters; and I think you'll have a pretty good handle on it [that is, they'll have enough information to pinpoint the landing site]. Generally, right now, we're sitting on a... [It's] not a level surface, but we don't see any particularly high hills, either. It's just sort of like an undulating plain? You can see quite far in all directions. There doesn't seem to be any particularly high objects such as mountains or high hills or anything like that that interferes with the view. The only features that are obvious, besides the just general rolling country that we're on, is the blocky rim craters that are visible in almost every direction. Some of them are quite close, and some of them are far away. We got one of them, for example, at 12 o'clock [that] Pete described. [It's] about 2000 or 3000 feet away, [that is, far enough] that if it didn't have these large boulders on it and had a pretty nice raised rim - perhaps maybe even up to [a] 10-feet-high raised rim - we wouldn't be able to see it. I guess the diameter of that crater must be on the order of 600 to 700 feet [actually about 1700 feet]. That's at 12 o'clock [west]. We've got a number of more weathered craters around us of every size: from one that's just outside the window here at 2 o'clock [out about] 15 feet that's about 6 feet in diameter and about 3 feet deep, all the way up to one [Middle Crescent Crater] that I see over at the 1 o'clock position. It doesn't have a particularly raised rim, but it looks like it could have a diameter in the order of 400 feet [or maybe] 500 feet [actually about 1500 feet]. [Pause] There are many rocks that are scattered around on the surface. Most of them are partially buried; and, as they are buried there, you can see that there are little fillets of dirt that has built up around almost all of them.

speaker: Bean
text: And I can't tell, of course, if it [the filleting]'s only from this direction or not [that is, he can only see the sides of the rocks facing the LM], but all these rocks seem to have the same characteristics, whether they are small or large. One interesting feature that is directly at our 12 o'clock, about 20 feet, is a whole surface area that's a bit different from the rest in the fact that it's got sort of parallel lines or parallel trenches or skin trenches perhaps an eighth of an inch deep and running what would be north to south to us; and you can see it from about my 2 or 3 o'clock position, all the way over to Pete's window. The left seems to... Some sort of force has apparently caused these traces to be made in the surface. I don't think it was our engine, because, as I say, they are perpendicular to the lines that our engine would have made. We'll be able to get a better look at that when we get out, of course; and we'll also be able to use that close-up stereo camera on it and just get some good pictures of it.

speaker: Gibson

speaker: Bean

There may be a chance to notice the contacts or different materials by looking at the texture: for example, that area that I described as directly in front of the LM that has those north-south lines on them. But, other than that, it just looks like one uniform surface with many, many craters in it. There's no immediately-apparent white-rim craters near us. Most of the ones that I can see out my window don't have a raised rim at all. They don't have any particular elongation. They seem to be - just from glancing at them - about the same texture as the areas surrounding them. [Pause]

speaker: Bean

It looks there are going to be some good places out here to the west to put the ALSEP.

speaker: Bean

This is a lot better surface, I think, than Pete or I had imagined before we got here. So I think, probably, with that we'll go ahead and start rigging out.

speaker: Conrad
text: I'll tell you what, Al...

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, Houston, I'm going to move the focus [on the TV] a bit and see what happens.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. Don't spend too much time on it. You're running a tad behind.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Well. I'll tell you what. I can feel that the wheel's...When I hold the end of the lens, I can feel the wheel's running, because I can feel something in motion inside. Okay. Now, I just changed completely the settings I had before. The f-stop's set at 22 but I can try something else.

speaker: Gibson
text: Okay, Al, we see no change down here. Why don't you press on?

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, let me try another f-stop, the other way. How's that?

speaker: Gibson
text: There's no change down here, Al. [Pause] That's coming in there, now, Al. Okay, what change did you make?

speaker: Bean
text: I hit it on the top with my hammer. I figured we didn't have a thing to lose.

speaker: Gibson
text: Skillful fix, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: I hit it on the top with this hammer I've got. [Responding to Gibson] Yeah, that's skilled craftsmanship. Got it [garbled]

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Al?

speaker: Bean
text: Yes, sir.

speaker: Conrad
text: That part has already sheared this thing.

speaker: Bean
text: Never touched it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: What should we do now with the lens, Houston?

speaker: Gibson
text: Okay; why don't you give us one more light rap [with the hammer], and also cut down on the f-stop?

speaker: Bean
text: All right. Will do. Now, is the zoom right for you? [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: [Garbled]

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, lord. [Pause] Need to jury rig [garbled under Gibson]...

speaker: Gibson
text: Al, we're still not getting a good picture. Why don't you press on, and we'll try to get back to it later, if we have time.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay; I'll pound it a little bit. [Pause] There you go. I'll just leave it like it is. Point it slightly toward the LM here, so that, if you do get a picture, you'll see something. There you go. That ought to give you some sort of a picture that you can think about. I'd be glad to come back and work on it. Got to go to work again.

speaker: Conrad
text: Al?

speaker: Bean
text: Yes, sir.

speaker: Conrad
text: What I need is a piece of tape.

speaker: Bean
text: Good luck.

speaker: Conrad
text: Boy, there's all kinds of tape around here.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [I've] had it on this thing. [Long Pause] Houston.

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, go ahead.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, the flag is [more or less] up.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, copy. The flag is up.

speaker: Conrad
text: We hope everyone down there is as proud of it as we are...

speaker: Gibson
text: We show you are very close to the nominal time line. How about a EMU check?

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. We have the flag up. Like I said, hope everybody down there is as proud of it as we are to put it up. [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: That's affirmative, Pete. And we're proud of what you're doing. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Al?

speaker: Bean
text: Yes, sir.

speaker: Conrad
text: Can we have a quickie [tourist photo] here?

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [To Al] Back up a little more ...

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: ...to about 15 feet.

speaker: Bean
text: All right. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Easy. You're getting into the TV cable!

speaker: Bean
text: Nope, I just went right over it, babe.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Laughs heartily]

speaker: Bean
text: Here you are. Take a look, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: I can't see you [because Al is standing up-Sun]. [Pause] Get it?

speaker: Bean
text: Sure did.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Pause] Another one?

speaker: Bean
text: Yeah.

speaker: Conrad
text: Wait one. [Pause] Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: Got you.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay; good.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, get back working.

speaker: Conrad
text: I go get my camera. I got some pan shots [to do] and next the ALSEP. [Pause] And, Houston, I'm down on Min cooling .

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. How's Al doing? [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Say again.

speaker: Gibson
text: Is Al doing all the work?

speaker: Conrad
text: No, sir. I'm heading out to do the pan photographs right now; and, with any luck at all, we'll get back on the timeline and complete what we need. Al's taking shots of the solar wind. And I'm hopping out here to the number 1 slot.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Bean
text: Boy, you sure can move on this surface.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah, but watch it when you hit a rock!

speaker: Bean
text: [Garbled].

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Pause] Go. f/11. f/11 it is. [Counting frames and clock positions as he turns] 1, 2, 3. Now f/8. [Pause] 4, 5, 6, 7 ... [Pause, possibly changing to f/5.6] 6, 7

speaker: Gordon
text: Hello, Houston. This is Yankee Clipper. I'm [garble].

speaker: Gibson
text: Clipper, you were broken up. Say again.

speaker: Conrad
text: Who are you talking to?

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, we have Clipper both - and you both on the same air-to-ground...

speaker: Gordon
text: Houston, this is Yankee Clipper.

speaker: Gibson
text: Clipper, go ahead. Say again.

speaker: Gordon
text: Houston, Yankee Clipper. I marked off Snowman with the telescope, and we're going to get some good pictures from that one.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Clipper.

speaker: Conrad
text: Six. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Do you hear a little background noise, Pete? Kind of staticky and things?

speaker: Conrad
text: I keep hearing a whistle.

speaker: Bean
text: That's what I hear. Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, Houston, two of the pans are done.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. Copy. Two pans. Al, how was the LM inspection?

speaker: Bean
text: I'm working on it right now.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [I'm] taking a look at that Surveyor, Al, I suspect we ought to be able to get there quite readily. I'm going to head down into the crater a little bit for this set of pans...Whoops, [garbled]

speaker: Bean
text: Watch yourself; it's easy to slide.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah, you can say that again. [Pause] I notice you've been over here, haven't you?

speaker: Bean
text: Uh-huh. [Garbled] [Pause] I don't think this is going to show anything, but I'll give it a go.

speaker: Conrad
text: What's that?

speaker: Bean
text: Oh, I'm trying to show the front gear there and how it planted itself, but it's not bright enough to [get a good photograph]. [Pause] Give it a go, though. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Uh-oh.

speaker: Bean
text: What happened?

speaker: Conrad
text: I think my camera's...[Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: This [foot]pad bounced. Could be your plus-Y [north footpad] bounced about a pad diameter.

speaker: Gibson
text: Al, do you have any comments on the footpad interaction with the surface?

speaker: Bean
text: Yes, I do. Actually, these pads went in a little bit further than did Neil's. I'd say most of the pads are in about an inch and a half to two; and it sort of looked like we were moving slightly forward [west], and had pretty well killed off our left/right velocity when we touched down. The right-hand [north] footpad seems to have bounced. That'd be the plus Y, the right-hand side one. The others don't seem to have. So it must have, maybe, hit there first, and rocked back and forth or something. [Garbled]

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. Do you see anything on the surface from the DPS [Descent Propulsion System, the descent engine]?

speaker: Bean
text: No, I don't. The surface under there...It's kind of interesting, the surface under there is clean. It doesn't have the loose dust particles as does the rest of the lunar surface about here. It also has a number of small round dirt clods, if you want, that seem to be rolling off in a radial direction from underneath the skirt of the engine. I'll take a couple of pictures [garbled] good shot, because the skirt's about 8 inches or so off the ground.

speaker: Gordon
text: Houston, Yankee Clipper. Do you have the DSKY?

speaker: Gibson
text: Stand by, Clipper.

speaker: Gibson
text: Clipper, Houston. We're watching the DSKY.

speaker: Bean
text: I think I can get a good one for you, Houston.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. It's good description.

speaker: Bean
text: There we go. Hey, you can really move around out here, Houston. That mobile POGO rig that we've got there, and also that one in the centrifuge. Man, it's just like this. You can just run and bounce just like you can on that POGO. It's a real good training device .

speaker: Conrad
text: Where are you, Al?

speaker: Bean
text: I'm over here [at] the back bay. I'm ready to start the ALSEP off-loading for 'em.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. I got something for you and I'm coming around.

speaker: Bean
text: All right.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Houston, I went back to Intermediate cooling .

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. We copy that.

speaker: Bean
text: Good idea. Say, I've noticed when you get started moving down here, well, it's sometimes hard to stop.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah. Hold on to this [probably Pete's saddlebag] a second...

speaker: Bean
text: All right.

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete and Al, you're 1 plus 22 into the timeline, and you're running about 6 minutes behind nominal. We're monitoring PLSS feedwater 2 as a determining parameter.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Houston. We'll start catching up now. We've kind of gotten over the initial checkout on how to walk and move around; and maybe we won't have any problem with this hardware like we did with the TV...

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled] Here you go.

speaker: Bean
text: ...and the [S-band] antenna.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. And we're showing 2 plus 30 left in the EVA.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause] Okay, Pete; your saddlebag's on.

speaker: Conrad
text: All right. Let's go.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. And we'll off-load the ALSEP. [Garbled].

speaker: Conrad
text: Nope. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: We ought to be able to move out with this thing.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: The experiment bay looks real good.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yup.

speaker: Bean
text: The LM exterior looks beautiful the whole way around. Real good shape. Not a lot that doesn't look the way it did the day we launched it.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Possibly pulling a lanyard to open the SEQ bay doors] Light one. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Here we go, Pete. Ohhhhh, up they go, babes. One ALSEP. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: There it is.

speaker: Bean
text: There it is, is right. [Now we] just lay it on the lunar surface. [Pause] Better go to intermediate cooling , get good and chilled down. [Pause] Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Wait a minute. [Garbled] You've got to go easy.

speaker: Bean
text: Sure do. [Pause] Here it [probably the first package] comes.

speaker: Conrad
text: Coming right out.

speaker: Bean
text: And just about right. Riding right out on the boom, Houston. Sure looks pretty.

speaker: Gibson
text: [Making a mis-identification] Roger, Pete. We copy. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: [Wanting to take a picture] Look at me, Pete. [Pause] It's a good shot, babe. The LM and everything's reflecting in your visor. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Lay her on the ground. Okay, I'll get mine out. [Long Pause] Right out on the boom, just like advertised.

speaker: Conrad
text: Wait until I get this [meaning the first ALSEP package] out of your way.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. Omni Charlie; Omni Charlie.

speaker: Gordon
text: [Garbled]

speaker: Conrad
text: It's going to look like...

speaker: Bean
text: Say again.

speaker: Conrad
text: Going to look like the back of the flight crew training building in a minute.

speaker: Bean
text: Uh-huh.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. SEQ Bay door is coming closed. [Pause] Uh-oh. It's all right. Push that door...[Pause] What am I hung up on.

speaker: Bean
text: I don't know. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Al, [garbled]. I have something [garbled]?

speaker: Bean
text: Let me look, Pete. [Pause] Here's one here. Let me get it off for you.

speaker: Conrad
text: Thank you. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, lift your left foot up and you're okay. [Pause] Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Thank you. [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. High Gain Antenna; Pitch, minus 13; Yaw, 225.

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, Houston, do you hear this constant beeping in the background?

speaker: Gibson
text: That's affirmative. We've heard it now for about the past 45 minutes.

speaker: Bean
text: What is it? [Responding to the second half of Gibson's communication] That's right, so have we. What is it?

speaker: Gibson
text: [Static returns briefly] Intrepid, we've tried to isolate it. It appears it's something on the downlink coming from the LM. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: Yes, sir. And there's the lunar tools all set up for you, fella.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: This ALSEP's doing okay. [Pause; static has cleared] Old Chuck Weatherred will be happy to know we're throwing it up for him, here. That's all right.

speaker: Conrad
text: Here you go. Now, what do you need of these?

speaker: Bean
text: I need anything you've got. [Garbled]...

speaker: Conrad
text: There you go.

speaker: Bean
text: ...that tool.

speaker: Conrad
text: How about this? You need that one?

speaker: Bean
text: How about the...Here, let me put that on. No, no. You put that in the package 2, and I'll pick that up later.

speaker: Conrad
text: It's already in package 2.

speaker: Bean
text: Then one must be yours.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. I put that there. [Pause] Excuse me, Pete, I'll move it [possibly the Hand Tool Carrier] over and plant it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Wait a minute.

speaker: Bean
text: All right.

speaker: Conrad
text: Got to put this together right. Where's the arrow? [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Shall I let down the cask while we wait?

speaker: Conrad
text: Wait a minute. Here you go.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: [I want to] put this together. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Houston, we're going to go ahead and pull down the fuel cask right now, and then I'll take the element out of it.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. Copy. You're working with the fuel cask.

speaker: Conrad
text: [To Al] Wait. Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait! [Laughs]

speaker: Bean
text: I knew it. That's a bad place to put it [the HTC?], Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Huh?

speaker: Bean
text: That's a bad place to put it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Fuel cask comes down beautifully. In position. Came down just right.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, I know what I have to do, Al. And I'm standing here not doing it.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, maybe I need to move the SIDE on.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: We're moving right along, Houston. We're catching up. [Long Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper; Houston. Go to Wide Deadband.

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston! You can log me for my first Boyd bolts on the Moon. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, Houston.

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, go ahead.

speaker: Bean
text: It's real interesting, as we put out this ALSEP right...[Hearing Gibson] There's one thing that's pretty obvious, as we're setting out the components of the ALSEP here. [And that] is: I just hope that these thermal coatings don't have to stay as white as they are right now, because there's just no way [of keeping them absolutely clean]. With all this dust, there's just no possibility...

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled]

speaker: Bean
text: ...of not getting them a little bit dirty. And...

speaker: Conrad
text: Little bit dirty isn't the word for it.

speaker: Bean
text: I know it. This is going to be a real problem, I guess, if thermally they've got to maintain that [clean] coating. Because there's just no way you can do it. Everything that touches the ground picks it up. Your suit is about half dirty because the [LEC] strap landed on it. Uh-oh. It's a little dirty even on top of the fuel element, there. Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Wait just a minute now before you get turned away.

speaker: Gibson
text: Al, we copy your comments.

speaker: Conrad
text: There. Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: I guess we'll just have to make allowances for things like that when we build them. They sure are going to get dirty. [Pause] Okay, I'm unlocking the cask dome , right now. It unlocked perfectly. Shaking it down, trying to get it off.

speaker: Conrad
text: There you go.

speaker: Bean
text: It came off beautifully. [I'll] put the tool and the dome aside.

speaker: Conrad
text: Very nice.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. I'll get out the cask removal tool. [Pause] Why don't you stand over there, Pete?

speaker: Conrad
text: I've got to go back to Min cooling . I'm about to freeze to death. [Garbled]

speaker: Bean
text: Yeah. Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Bean
text: I am.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh.

speaker: Bean
text: Yeah; it's not...[Pause] There you go. [Pause] Sliding right in there. Okay, tighten up the lock [garbled]. Hold it. [Long Pause] You got to be kidding.

speaker: Conrad
text: Make sure it [the removal tool]'s screwed all the way down. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: That could make a guy mad, you know it?

speaker: Conrad
text: Yup. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Let me undo it a minute, and try it a different way.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yup. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: It can really get you mad.

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston, Al put the tool on, screwed it all the way down, and the fuel element would not come out of the cask. He's taking the tool off, and he's working her again.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. We copy. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [To Houston] [You] guys got any suggestions?

speaker: Bean
text: It really kind of surprises me. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled] come over and look.

speaker: Bean
text: I tell you what worries me, Pete. If I pull on it too hard, it's a very delicate lock mechanism. Maybe [I should] not push the pins in quite so far, and wiggle it a little. I just get the feeling that it's hot and swelled in there or something. Doesn't want to come out. I can sure feel the heat, though, on my hands. [Pause] Come out of there! Rascal. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Suppose it outgassed or something? [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Say, Houston?

speaker: Gibson
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. We've really got a problem, I guess. I've tried using different pins... You know, it's got a three-pin removal tool, so I tried using different pins in different holes. That doesn't appear to have any effect. You know, everything operates just exactly like it does in the training mock-ups and up at GE [General Electric Corporation]. The only problem is, it just won't come out of the cask. I am suspicious that it's just swollen in there or something and friction's holding it in. But it's such a delicate tool, I really hate to pull on it too hard.

speaker: Bean
text: I think what we can do...

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, I'll be with you.

speaker: Bean
text: ...go get that hammer and bang on the side of it.

speaker: Conrad
text: No. I got a better idea. Where's the hammer?

speaker: Bean
text: That's what I said.

speaker: Conrad
text: No, no. But I want to try and put the back end in under that lip there and pry her out. Let me go get the hammer. Be right back. Where did you put it?

speaker: Bean
text: Huh? What? Hammer's on the MESA.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Let me get the tool off; it's starting to warm up.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Can't figure that out. [Long Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Al, when you're working on that, try to make sure you've got the pins all the way in. Tighten up on it; then you can try pushing down on it a little, before you pull it out.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [To Pete] Don't touch these needles [the pins on the removal tool]; if these break off, that's all she wrote.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah. I understand.

speaker: Bean
text: And don't pound on anything [garbled].

speaker: Conrad
text: No, no. I'm not going to.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause] We'll try again. Rotate and try it this way. [Pause] [The removal tool] drives in there just like it's going to do the job. Only it doesn't do the job.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh man, look at this dust fly. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Just a minute. Just a minute. [Let me] get those pins in there again. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: You're not getting those pins all the way in.

speaker: Bean
text: They're not in now because I'm lining them up. Just a damn minute. Now they are all the way in. They're all the way...Not quite. That bottom one down there's...[Pause] Now, my recommendation would be pound on the casket, then...you know.

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, that's doing it! Give it a few more pounds. [Pause] Got to beat harder than that. [Pause] Keep going. It's coming out. It's coming out! [Pause] Pound harder.

speaker: Conrad
text: Keep going.

speaker: Bean
text: [Laughs, cheering him on] Come on, Conrad!

speaker: Conrad
text: Keep going, baby.

speaker: Bean
text: That hammer's a universal tool.

speaker: Conrad
text: You better believe it...

speaker: Bean
text: There, you got it!

speaker: Conrad
text: Got it.

speaker: Bean
text: Got it, Houston. [Pete giggles] That's beautiful. That's too much.

speaker: Gibson
text: Well done, troops.

speaker: Conrad
text: I gotta go put the...

speaker: Bean
text: We got it, babe! It fits in the RTG real well! It's just the cask was holding it in on the side.

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. One minute to LOS.

speaker: Bean
text: Don't come to the Moon without a hammer. [Pause] That's it, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Laughing]

speaker: Bean
text: Outstanding!

speaker: Conrad
text: [Laughing; Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Let's make our move [and carry the ALSEP out to the deployment site].

speaker: Conrad
text: I'm ready. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: That cask's going [in?]. Okay, Houston. The fuel element is in the RTG . I can feel it radiate heat already! [To Pete] Put your hand over here.

speaker: Gibson
text: Copied that, Al.

speaker: Conrad
text: Wait a minute; don't move...No, wait a minute, Al. Have you got a strap around your boot? Let me look and see.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: No. You're all right.

speaker: Bean
text: All right?

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah.

speaker: Bean
text: Boy, this thermal coating doesn't mean a thing here [because it gets dirty so quickly].

speaker: Conrad
text: Uh-huh. That thing is really getting covered with dirt.

speaker: Bean
text: Gosh! I hope they made allowances for it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Me, too. Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. You're in, pal.

speaker: Bean
text: It doesn't look like it [is properly attached]. Let me look at that just a second.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: It's the right way. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: That's it.

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, feel the heat off that machine. That's amazing.

speaker: Conrad
text: 1400 degrees [Fahrenheit or about 760 Celsius]. [In a conspiratorial tone] Almost as hot as the Sun! [Chuckles]

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, do me a favor.

speaker: Conrad
text: What do you need? No, go lower. There you go. You got it.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay; let me go scout...smoke over the area.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Got everything you need?

speaker: Conrad
text: [Examining his cuff checklist entry at 1+36 ] All right, there's no TV, so I got the SIDE [subpallet] and the picker-uppers for the rocks [meaning the tongs]!

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Let's go right off to our little mound over there; how does that grab you?

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Now, something's wrong.

speaker: Conrad
text: What's the matter? [Long Pause, probably while they make sure the packages are secure on the carrybar]

speaker: Bean
text: Well, it's kinda...The thing doesn't...Well, let's try it.

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, we copy. You've got the UHT, tongs, and [SIDE] subpallet.

speaker: Bean
text: We're making our move, Houston. I can tell this is going to be a workload. I'll take it easy.

speaker: Conrad
text: [To Houston] How long did you say our shadow was...[that is], the LM's shadow, 150 feet?

speaker: Gibson
text: Stand by, Pete.

text: Yeah. You're in good shape. That doesn't have to level, huh?

speaker: Bean
text: No, because the other one levels on this stool.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Push it down a little bit.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. That's a good idea.

speaker: Conrad
text: Seat it. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Looking good. Looking good.

speaker: Conrad
text: Just give me the tongs, and I'll put them away.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Get with it and I'll start opening Boyd bolts . [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Yup. That's going to do okay, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Thank you.

speaker: Bean
text: Yeah.

speaker: Conrad
text: All righty. [Long Pause] If I wasn't at 3.7 psi, I'd whistle while I work. I can't do it. [Four, short, monotonic, breathy attempts] [Garbled; Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. That seismometer's right in position now. Here's hoping...here's hoping nothing happens to it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Looks real good, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: Yeah, it does. It looks like it's going to clear. Houston, looks like digging that little hole might work. Setting up there nice now. And it looks like maybe it's not going to get down in the hole. Maybe we did it. Let's just see.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. We concur; it sounds like a good plan. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Whoops. [Pause] You know something? Look at that.

speaker: Conrad
text: What?

speaker: Bean
text: Well, I [should] put a little dirt on it, I guess. When I put out the skirt of this foil, it doesn't want to lie down. I guess because it's been folded so long. I guess I can probably just spread it out. [Pete chuckles; Pause] It acts almost like it gets a little static charge on it. It's resisting the lunar surface. I'm sure that isn't it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, stop one second.

speaker: Bean
text: Watch out. Don't come across...

speaker: Conrad
text: I know. That's why [what] I want you to do is come take it.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: That [connecting] cable isn't even unreeling. See, it's perfect. Take it out there and set it. That a boy.

speaker: Bean
text: It's right behind there. You may...

speaker: Conrad
text: There you go.

speaker: Bean
text: ...want to just take it. [Pause] You might want to trip it off that thing, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Trip it off what?

speaker: Bean
text: It's on that post.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh. All right. [Pause] [I see] what you're talking about. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: [Aligning the PSE or setting the magnetometer down] That shadow's going to be just right. Looking okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Ah, fiddle dee diddle. Come on. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, everything is going great, but that whistle [on the comm circuit] is driving me nuts. Bothering you?

speaker: Bean
text: A little bit. [Pause] Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, darn! I can't help but get dirt on this darn thing, no matter how careful I am.

speaker: Bean
text: I don't think there's a way, Pete. I don't think there's a way. [Pause] Unless you got, you know, where you could put it out in a package and then your last step - like the SIDE over there - it just deploys off the thermal wrapping - or your dirt protector - and you end up with a nice, clean experiment sitting there. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: How we doing on the timeline, Houston?

speaker: Gibson
text: Stand by, Pete. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Wheee! [Hearty Laugh]

speaker: Bean
text: What happened?

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, it's just the way things [one of the Boyd bolts ] pop off down here in one-sixth g. [Pause] Won't be long and I'll get to my favorite task, pointing the [Central Station] antenni [sic].

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, we show you're about 8 to 10 minutes behind but it's no sweat. You've got lots of oxygen and feedwater. We'll give you an update on the time remaining when you finish deploying ALSEP.

speaker: LM Crew
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: Good. Looks like it's going real good. Houston. [On] this seismometer, I'm having a little trouble making the skirt lie down; but, other than that, it looks good. It doesn't want to just lay flat like it does on Earth at one g. It sort of wants to slip up. I guess it's just because it's this memory in it from being folded so long, and...

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. You can make a two-man task out of that and put a little dirt around the outside edge to hold it down if you like. [Pause] You won't have any trouble getting a little dirt on it, will you?

speaker: Bean
text: Houston, I noticed that if I just... [Pause, hearing the second part of Gibson's remark] I'm pushing it down. [Pause] That'll do it. [Pause] Okay, Pete. Let me level it [the PSE] up. I think it's pretty near level. It's lined up exactly. [Pause] See if I can give it a couple of pushes.

speaker: Conrad
text: I got this feeling there's a couple of Boyd bolts that I haven't done here [garbled]. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: This thing looks level as can be to me. [Pause] Looks good.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. Copy. You have the bubble centered. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: I'll tell you an interesting thing about this bubble, Houston. [Pause] No. It's okay. It's okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Slowly enunciating each word] I am not happy here, Al. I'm afraid some of these Boyd bolts...There's not enough of them, and I don't understand why.

speaker: Bean
text: Why, one of them didn't do or what?

speaker: Conrad
text: Well, I don't know. I haven't the foggiest idea. I thought all of them did.

speaker: Bean
text: Looked like you're well ahead of the time.

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, take your stick and kick a little dirt up on it right there [on the skirt].

speaker: Conrad
text: Huh?

speaker: Bean
text: Take your stick and just put a little dirt on the edge. Just on the edge, though. Not much. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Uh-oh. [Garbled] bad news.

speaker: Bean
text: That's okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: I won't do that anymore.

speaker: Bean
text: That's okay; that skirt'll stay down enough. [Pause] Okay. That's complete. Let me take a couple of pictures. [Pause] Okay. Houston. The passive seismic is down; the alignment is exactly 90 degrees. And I'm going to take a couple pictures of it here.

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: Yes, sir?

speaker: Conrad
text: I don't know what's the matter, but something is...There it is. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Hey; look and see if the lens on my camera looks clean?

speaker: Conrad
text: Huh? Wait a minute. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: There, you got it made.

speaker: Conrad
text: No, I don't either. I don't know what's the matter.

speaker: Bean
text: Want me to hold down this part while you get that other bolt?

speaker: Conrad
text: Push that center down.

speaker: Bean
text: All right. Oops.

speaker: Conrad
text: There it is.

speaker: Bean
text: You got it. That's beautiful.

speaker: Conrad
text: Easy. [Sustained laugh]

speaker: Bean
text: Man alive. It sure wants to come up, doesn't it? Whoo!

speaker: Conrad
text: That did it.

speaker: Bean
text: That's beautiful.

speaker: Conrad
text: That did it. [Pause] Houston, Central Station's up.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. Copy. Central Station up and [confirming Al's report on the PSE alignment] 90 degrees on the PSE gnomon. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: Yes, sir. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Never mind. I'll get you in a minute.

speaker: Bean
text: Uh-oh. Don't ever move backwards.

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, we're going to have to do a lot of... [Pause] What did you do, fall over?

speaker: Bean
text: No.

speaker: Conrad
text: No?

speaker: Bean
text: No, but I just... I didn't even come close, actually. It's just that I think it [his warning about moving backward]'s something you want to follow as a rule. [Pause] But don't kick dirt on this [garbled] right there.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled under Al] right there. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled] One problem [is that] the Central Station is not really level. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Not too bad.

speaker: Bean
text: [I'll] get a good shot of it here, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. I'll take out the magnetometer. [Pause] Central Station went up so nice.

speaker: Conrad
text: Al, those are my last two Boyd bolts .

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Long Pause] I'm down in a little crater now, Houston. And, sure enough, right in the bottom of the crater there is a lot softer dust than up on the rim. Not much; but it's noticeable. I don't think the sides are slippery at all. I don't think it's going to bother us going over to get our Surveyor.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. We copy.

speaker: Gibson
text: Are you on your way out with the LSM [Lunar Surface Magnetometer]?

speaker: Bean
text: That's right. Got it right in hand; I'm out at the end of the line [50 ft SSE of the Central Station], and I'm deploying the legs right now.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: One antenna mast in place, Houston. Going back for my favorite thing.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. Copy antenna mast in place and good luck.

speaker: Conrad
text: What'd you...

speaker: Bean
text: Look at that, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: What?

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, one of the fun things here, Houston, is all these Styrofoam packing blocks that are put on there to protect it during shipment or launch. When you take them off and throw them, they really sail. These things stay airborne up for 10 seconds, maybe. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Got any more thoughts on our TV camera, Houston?

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, Pete? Pete?

speaker: Conrad
text: What?

speaker: Bean
text: Watch this. [They both laugh, probably as they watch another piece of Styrofoam sail off into the distance].

speaker: Bean
text: Try that on... Hey, I just threw something. It hasn't hit the ground yet; it might have gone up 300 feet. [Pete laughs] Boing!

speaker: Conrad
text: [Laughing] Stop playing and get to work. [Laughing]. Come on. Maybe they'll extend us until 4-1/2 hours. I feel like I could stay out here all day.

speaker: Bean
text: I know it.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled] holds up. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Right there. This is going to be a good place for the magnetometer.

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, we've been thinking on that [TV] camera, and when you get back [to the LM], we'll have a test for you to run on it. It looks as though part of it's come back. And we're going to try and see what we can salvage.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: What do you think happened to it, Houston? [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Al, we're not sure on that. Why don't you wait until you get back to the LM, and we'll work it out a bit and see if we can determine it?

speaker: Bean
text: All right.

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, Al?

speaker: Bean
text: Yes.

speaker: Conrad
text: See, that nice ...

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, that's weird. [They both laugh] On Earth, they [magnetometer arms] just flop out in position. Here they don't even want to stay. There they go.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Chuckling] That thing hit the ground and it's still bouncing. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: [Pleased with how easily the magnetometer is deploying] That's slick. That's really slick! [Pause] Boy, I hope... I hope... [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Hello, Yankee Clipper; Houston.

speaker: Conrad
text: You hope, you hope?

speaker: Bean
text: Oh, I was just thinking about something. [Pause] Pete, no way to keep these things clean; I'm really worried about this white coating. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Lucky for me that this antenna head is almost [pause] level. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: You see that? The dot doesn't... It's hard to see. I'll see what I can do with it. [Pause] There it is. There it is! I think. Right there. [The level bubble is] right in the center. Center. [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston.

speaker: Gordon
text: Hello, Houston; Clipper here.

speaker: Gibson
text: Dick, the EVA - EVA is going pretty well; they're 2½ hours into it; and they've, got the ALSEP a good way deployed. Apparently both of them look as though they just crawled out of a coal bin. Other than that, seems pretty much nominal.

speaker: Gordon
text: Very good. Thank you.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, Houston. The magnetometer's deployed; it's level; and it's pointed exactly east. And the little black dot is right in the middle.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. Copy.

speaker: Bean
text: Same concern here [is that] there's just a lot of dust on top of the box where the electronics are. Just hope it doesn't bother it too much.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. Yankee Clipper, we have a map update for Rev 19. [Pause.]

speaker: Gordon
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, Pete, let me take a couple of pictures of this. Ack! I'm really...

speaker: Conrad
text: What are you mumbling about over there?

speaker: Bean
text: Well, I just don't like all that dirt on it; don't know what we can do, though. There's no way to work around it. The radiator's got a little dirt on it, and there's no way to dust it off, there's no way to... All you can do is tap it a little bit and hope some of it falls off and that's about it. Don't want to tap it too hard. [Pause] That's the best I can do. Okay, [that's finished]. [Long Pause while he takes the pictures]

speaker: Bean
text: God damn. [Pause] Okay; I'll deploy the SIDE, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: It's my last item [on the ALSEP portion of the checklist].

speaker: Conrad
text: [I'm] on my last one.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Does the antenna look like it's pointed at Earth?

speaker: Bean
text: It looks close.

speaker: Conrad
text: That's it. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [I'll] do the SIDE, right now. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [Still getting the antenna aligned] Got it.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause] Okay. I hope I don't tug on the [Central] station here [with the SIDE cable] as I come out, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: If that happens...

speaker: Bean
text: It looks pretty level, by the way. Your station does.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: I'm nearing the end [of the SIDE cable], I'll bet.

speaker: Conrad
text: I'm done. How's that, ah,... [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Gosh, this... [Laughing] They must have doubled the cable length on this one.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled] [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: That's it.

speaker: Conrad
text: You're at the end. You're at the end.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Let me set it down and work on it right here.

speaker: Conrad
text: That does it, old buddy.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Now what do I want to do? [Long Pause as he consults his checklist]

speaker: Bean
text: [Doesn't] want to do like that, does it?

speaker: Conrad
text: [Did you] pick up the tongs?

speaker: Bean
text: What?

speaker: Conrad
text: Pick up the tongs? Were they with that [SIDE] box? Or do I have them?

speaker: Bean
text: You've probably got them on you.

speaker: Conrad
text: I do.

speaker: Bean
text: I can't see... No, they weren't with that box. We used them for something by your Central Station. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Ah, yeah, I got them on me.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, Houston, the antenna is up. It's aligned to [pointing angles] 1644 and 525.

speaker: Gibson
text: We copy that, Pete. You got the nominal alignment. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: That came out. SIDE screen came out very nice.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: Popped it out. Looks good.

speaker: Conrad
text: Boy, are you dirty. [Pause] I'm just as dirty.

speaker: Bean
text: Doesn't much want to stay down.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Commenting on the ease of antenna pointing] Okay. That first [garbled]; I can't believe it. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: [Laughing] You got to be kidding.

speaker: Conrad
text: What?

speaker: Bean
text: Boy, anytime you put anything spring-loaded on the Moon you're in trouble. [Pete laughs] This screen has got sort of, you know, a spring to it? Doesn't want to lie down much up here in this gravity.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Houston, how long we been out?

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, you've been out 2 plus 40, and the pacing one right now is Al [because he is not yet finished with the SIDE deployment]. You're running around 20 minutes behind. And when you can, we'd like an EMU check, and if you'd give us your O2 readings?

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. My O2 reading is 50 percent. And have you got anything for us? Haven't heard too much from you.

speaker: Gibson
text: Negative on that. You're perking along real well. And we're following your progress. It looks as though you're getting the job done.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Look... How you doing, Al?

speaker: Bean
text: I'm doing good.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: That little thing just doesn't want to...

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston, let me ask you a question. Can I push in the shorting amps thing?

speaker: Gibson
text: That's affirmative, Pete. We understand you're not able to get a reading. So, go ahead and close it, and we'll stand by for a zero reading.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Responding to the first part of Gibson's reply] All right. You might... [Responding to the second part] Okay, it might be full scale high.

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, you'd better tell them I still haven't put the SIDE down.

speaker: Conrad
text: That doesn't make any difference, does it?

speaker: Bean
text: I don't know.

speaker: Conrad
text: It's all connected. [To Gibson] It's all connected. Does it make any difference, Houston?

speaker: Gibson
text: Stand by. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: You're a big area litter bug. [Laughing] You know that?

speaker: Bean
text: I know it. [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, we'd like you to go ahead and get the full deployment done first before you depress the shorting amps.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [To Al] Boy, you're dirty all the way to your knees. Can I give you any help?

speaker: Bean
text: Sure could.

speaker: Conrad
text: All right; here I come. [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: And, Pete and Al, a comment on picture taking. If you would, try to document some of the dirt which has gotten all over the equipment. If you would, try to get close-ups which will show the dirt we might have on thermally-sensitive areas. And, also, when you get done, if you would, take one or two extra pictures showing the ALSEP with the mounds that you described previously in the background. That'll give us a good geometric reference.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. I did a pan...

speaker: Bean
text: Hold that, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: I did a pan out here at the...

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Just a second. Now, let me hold this end and you stretch that end out.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. I got it.

speaker: Bean
text: Go to the right. That's it. Get the coils out of it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Which way's that thing head?

speaker: Bean
text: It's got to head away from the Central Station; away from everything. Probably ought to be a point right over there.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: But, now, I think if you kind of twirled it a couple times, it would end up uncoiling that twist in the line there. [Pause] That's the right way. Try it that way again. Looks like it might be working. [Pause] That's good. That's doing good! Okay. Let me take and set this thing down, and it's supposed to point to the Earth this way. That'll be good.

speaker: Conrad
text: Get your ground wires wrapped around the legs.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, I got it. Looks like it's going to be okay.

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston.

speaker: Gordon
text: Go ahead.

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, if you'll give P00 and Accept, we'll ship you up a state vector, a target load, and a REFSMMAT.

speaker: Bean
text: Put it down.

speaker: Gordon
text: You['ve] got it.

speaker: Gordon
text: [Garble] has got it.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Hold on; hold on. [Talking to the experiment package] Don't tip over.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah; wait a minute, wait a minute.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: I got it steadied.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: There, that's all right.

speaker: Bean
text: Just hold it there just a...

speaker: Conrad
text: Watch it, watch it, watch it.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. I'm trying to.

speaker: Conrad
text: No, your foot's hung in it. That a boy.

speaker: Bean
text: That did it. Okay. Let me sneak it back on again. Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Now, what do you want?

speaker: Bean
text: I want to put that [SIDE] lid back on there. [But] it would probably be best if we just left it off.

speaker: Conrad
text: I think it would be best if you left it alone.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Now, you hold it there [either with his foot or a tool] while I [garbled]...

speaker: Conrad
text: I got it. I got it anchored.

speaker: Bean
text: ...because this [the CCIG he is manipulating] is going to want to turn it [the SIDE] over.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah. I know.

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. We're coming up with a load.

speaker: Gordon
text: Yeah.

speaker: Conrad
text: Step on it [either the cable or the CCIG].

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. That's what I think I can do.

speaker: Conrad
text: Those guys got to be kidding about that cable on the... I knew that thing was going to do that. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: There, maybe that's better. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Come on, this thing's making us run behind.

speaker: Bean
text: I know it, but I don't see any way to quickly get...

speaker: Conrad
text: [Laughing] All right; now, just a minute. Move your foot. [Pause] That's better.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Let me just try it a couple more times. I think if I hold it this way and use this tool, I can probably set it...

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, it's just like zero g; everything floats up. That baby's going to nose dive into the dirt every time, sure as I'm standing here. That cable's cleverly designed to make it do that.

speaker: Bean
text: Let's put it like this. [Pause] Down like that.

speaker: Conrad
text: Don't fall over.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause] There's no way [to get it properly oriented].

speaker: Conrad
text: Uh-uh. Just... That a boy. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: That thing goes right in the dirt each time...

speaker: Conrad
text: I know, I know. It's going to do that. It's very frustrating. Turn it around and point it the other way. See if it'll point out that way.

speaker: Bean
text: All right. That might be good, too. Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: I knew that ding-a-ling cable was going to make us spend hours trying to do that.

speaker: Bean
text: [Laughing] Doesn't that make you mad?

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah; I know. Especially when you know it's going to happen.

speaker: Bean
text: Look, why can't I set it like this? You just let go of the SIDE and come over and step on that thing.

speaker: Conrad
text: Hey, if this SIDE falls over, then I'm really going to be mad. I got that thing firmly planted.

speaker: Bean
text: Just a minute. Wait, wait. Hold it, hold it. Hold her a minute. Okay. If I can get this just arranged.

speaker: Conrad
text: That's it. Now step on it.

speaker: Bean
text: I can't. There's no way.

speaker: Conrad
text: Let go of the string in your hand. That a boy. Now stand...

speaker: Bean
text: It's just...

speaker: Conrad
text: [Talking to the equipment] Don't flop. That's it. Push it in.

speaker: Bean
text: Ah! We made it. I hope. Let's push it real hard in there.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: I think we've got it licked.

speaker: Conrad
text: That a boy. Easy does it.

speaker: Bean
text: [As the experiment falls over again] Aw, you... The thing just jumps right up. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: [Laughing]

speaker: Bean
text: Pete, I'm just afraid that one's... We've had it on this one.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Laughing] You've had it on that one, my friend.

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, here it is here. Look; I don't think it makes any difference if it lays on its side as long as it points its aperture in the right place.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah.

speaker: Bean
text: Let's move it around here and just let it lay on its side. [Pause] You know, it doesn't know the difference. [Pause] Just kind of lay it around. Just try to... Yeah; that'll work; that'll work.

speaker: Gibson
text: Al, we concur with that. Go ahead.

speaker: Conrad
text: That work right there?

speaker: Bean
text: [Responding to Gibson] Okay. It looks like the only way... This cable has just got too much spring for the weight of the package, and there's just no way. Okay, Pete. Let her go. Now, let me level it [the SIDE]. [Pause] No way [is the CCIG going to deploy properly].
