speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. We copy that.

speaker: Conrad
text: And they are constantly underfoot. [See AS12-46- 6867 ] [Pause] All right. Al, let me take it [the LEC] across to the other side [possibly to outside the south porch rail] so it's out of your way.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Gibson
text: Al, before egress, would you confirm that the TV circuit breaker is out?

speaker: Bean
text: Confirmed; out.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Bean
text: It is out, Houston.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, my friendly gnomon. In all the [garbled] activity yesterday, I forgot all about him sitting here.

speaker: Conrad
text: What you up to, Al?

speaker: Bean
text: Getting this [16 mm sequence] camera set.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Got SRC 2. [Pause] Working away here. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Let me check all the circuit breakers and I'll be out with you.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay on that side. [Pause] And 11 [Pete's CB panel] now. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: I'll tell you, these Teflon bags don't hold up too well in a vacuum. In a lunar environment; I'll put it that way.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. We copy that comment. Any clarification?

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah, they tend to have fatigue failures along the cracks [that is, along the side folds] when you go to open them up. I notice the two bags that I put in the SRC yesterday were that way. And, let me get back here [into the sunlight] just a second. Let's see. [Reading] Pass LEC; ETB transfer; geology Prep; stow on HTC: contrast charts, extension handle, hammer, small shovel, and gnomon.

speaker: Bean
text: Here I come. Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, have fun. [Reading] Place SRC 2 on MESA; attach weigh bag to scale; attach saddlebag to LMP. There's one thing that's bothering me; I don't have that saddlebag. I wonder why I don't? Where might I find one? [Pause] Ah, ha, ha! Here's one. [To Al] How are you doing?

speaker: Bean
text: Good.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Offering to watch Al come out through the hatch] Let me check. Okay. Keep coming. Super good shape. There you go. A little left. [Garbled under Al]

speaker: Bean
text: Wait a minute while I try to close this hatch.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, okay. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Right now, this stuff...[correcting himself] this material around the spacecraft reminds me...In this Sun angle, looking into the Sun, [it's] a very rich brown color, [and it] kind of reminds me of a good plowed field.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Looking down-Sun, it's still the same old ash gray; very light, white, ash gray. [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. LMP's off the footpad.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, LMP. How about let's get a Surveyor parts bag here?

speaker: Bean
text: All right. Just a second, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: All right.

speaker: Bean
text: Pull down my blinders.

speaker: Conrad
text: Huh?

speaker: Bean
text: I'm going to pull down those little side visors.

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston. I think Al and I both find that these little side Sun visors are extremely handy.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. We copy.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled] this strap down [on the Surveyor parts bag]. [Long Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Almost cold today [in the LM shadow] on mid-cooling. How are you doing?

speaker: Bean
text: About the same. [Garbled] that line right there, Pete.

speaker: Conrad
text: Say again.

speaker: Bean
text: I'm going to set the tether [safety line] right there and...

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay; and I'll put it [the Surveyor parts bag] on you here, babe.

speaker: Conrad
text: How's that? [Do] you want me to stand low or high?

speaker: Bean
text: Low.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. How's that?

speaker: Bean
text: Good. Okay, got that one on - [garbled] the side. Looking good so far. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: You know, other than the large-size rocks, [it's] very, very difficult to determine a contact around here. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay; [garbled]. [Pause] Okay. Go around to the side. We're putting the parts bag on Pete right now, Houston.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Garbled, possibly Hold on.]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. I will.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. We copy that.

speaker: Conrad
text: Boy, Houston. That Comm is super; it sounds like you're right inside my helmet.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. It's the best sim[ulated EVA] we've had.

speaker: Bean
text: I wonder what happened since yesterday?

speaker: Conrad
text: I don't know. I think everybody learns a little bit...

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: ...each time.

speaker: Bean
text: That bag's on there; now, let's see what else [is on the checklist].

speaker: Conrad
text: I need to get the [bolt-cutting] tool. Hold the phone. [Pause] And before you put the tool in [the Surveyor parts bag], we got to cut a TV cable.

speaker: Gibson
text: That's affirmative. Cut the TV cable below the adapter, about 1 inch and then...[correcting himself] that's 1 foot below the adapter, and then stow the TV camera in the ETB.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Long Pause] Hey, look at that Surveyor, Al. That's not anywheres near as bad a slope [as it had seemed during EVA-1].

speaker: LM Crew
text: [Garbled] shade.

speaker: Bean
text: Hey, Houston, that Surveyor looks a lot better today.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah, now that the Sun's up on it.

speaker: Bean
text: Get some Sun on it. [Garbled] yesterday.

speaker: Conrad
text: Get those TV cables cut. Al, wait a minute; leave it [the TV camera] right on there [on the tripod] for a second. Come on over and put the thing [the bolt cutter] in my back [that is, in the parts bag] and let's mount our [Hasselblad] cameras and then the ETB is empty [to receive the TV camera].

speaker: Bean
text: All right. Sounds good.

speaker: Conrad
text: Or either that, [or] bring it [the TV camera] back...I'm sorry.

speaker: Bean
text: It's okay. Doesn't make any difference. [Garbled] [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: I think you got the right...

speaker: Bean
text: Here.

speaker: Conrad
text: ...got the right idea. That's the lunar walk.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Stick it in here.

speaker: Conrad
text: Look at that part number on the side of the tool. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: [Chuckling] Use that a few times.

speaker: Conrad
text: Say, Houston, while he's putting the tool on, it's a very interesting thing. There is a angular rock that's literally 6 inches from the engine exhaust skirt. It's just sitting on the lunar surface; and I really find it hard to believe that the engine exhaust couldn't blow that rock away. It's only about 3-1/2 inches by 3-1/2 inches; and it's not stuck in the ground; it's just sitting there loosely about 6 inches from the engine bell; and, of course, the ground is blasted clean all the way around it and yet the engine exhaust blast didn't blow that rock away.

speaker: Bean
text: Pete, where's the saddlebag?

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. We copied that comment. Were you able to get a photo of that in the first EVA?

speaker: Conrad
text: No, we'll get that right now. Is there one [that is, a saddlebag] in here, Al?

speaker: Bean
text: Yeah.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh. [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: And, Pete and Al, for your reference on the photos, your shadow length now is 18 foot.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [To Pete] Here's a couple of sneaky bags [that is, saddlebags] for us.

speaker: Gibson
text: Al, also if you would, before you start that traverse, would you get a good photo of the solar wind to show us how that foil is wrapped around?

speaker: Bean
text: Will do. Okay, Houston, that won't take a second. Okay, let me attach this bag to...Would you attach this bag to me, Pete?

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: I'm going to slide that off at the same time.

speaker: Conrad
text: All right. [Pause] Okay, I'll tell you what, if you go put one camera...Here, the saddlebag's on...if you'd put one [70mm Hasselblad] camera on...

speaker: Bean
text: Look at those little...

speaker: Conrad
text: ...Go get the TV, I'll mount this other gear on here [that is, on the HTC]. My compliments to the man that packed that SRC box; it looks just like the training boxes.

speaker: Bean
text: Hand me those tongs a second.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yes, sir. Here's the tongs. [Pause] Where are you?

speaker: Bean
text: Right behind you. Wait; hold on just a second. Hold on; let's see what this is.

speaker: Conrad
text: That's what left of...

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, got you.

speaker: Conrad
text: ...one of those parts bags [he may mean the remnants of a weigh bag].

speaker: Bean
text: Got you. Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay; core tubes. [Pause] [Talking to the core tube] Come on; get out of there. If I didn't know better, I'd say there was solar wind up here [pause] that blows hard enough to blow sample bags in the wrong direction. [Pause] Okay, Al, three core tubes in the deal [that is, in the HTC].

speaker: Bean
text: Okay; [garbled].

speaker: Conrad
text: Dixie cup dispenser coming up. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Could you [garbled]? [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Saddlebag. [Pause] Chart fits right in its spot. Worried about that. Got it?

speaker: Conrad
text: Yes, sir. It's in the saddlebag.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Now here's the other thing here.

speaker: Bean
text: That safety line.

speaker: Conrad
text: Huh? Oh, yeah. [Pause] Why don't I hook those on there, too. That thing [probably the pack of flat sample bags]'s a pain in the neck over there, the way they spread out in the vacuum.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: And I got the gas sample tube here.

speaker: Bean
text: All right.

speaker: Conrad
text: Gas sample tube coming up.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. Now I need to get that safety line. Okay; I'll put that over here.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, I'll get the safety line. One safety line...Whoops, excuse me.

speaker: Bean
text: That's okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: I'll put my [70mm] camera on; we'll put the TV camera in the ETB; and away we go.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay; we need to take...

speaker: Conrad
text: Here.

speaker: Bean
text: All right.

speaker: Conrad
text: Wait a...Right there. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Got it?

speaker: Conrad
text: Yes, sir. It's in.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. If you get your [70mm] camera, I'll put that TV camera in the ETB.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: Per their request. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, from the local terrain, Houston, as you know it right now, and with the polarizing filter, have you got any particular place enroute to the ALSEP or to Head Crater that you'd like any polarizing pictures taken?

speaker: Gibson
text: We'll get back to you on that. Press on now with the nominal plan right now.

speaker: Conrad
text: [To Al] Here, let me have it [the TV camera].

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, let me fold the handle.

speaker: Conrad
text: Fold the handle, yeah. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Hold it tight.

speaker: Conrad
text: I got it as far as I can. [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, we have no preference on that. [That is, Houston has no preference with regard to a location for the pictures to be taken with the polarizing filter.] Go ahead and take it as called out for in the cuff checklist.

speaker: Conrad
text: [To Al] Okay. Stick it in the ETB and we'll screw with it [meaning the TV] later.

speaker: Bean
text: Good idea.

speaker: Conrad
text: Handle in.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Don't] drop her. Okay, Houston, one TV camera in the bag. And our plan of attack is...Al?

speaker: Bean
text: Go.

speaker: Conrad
text: [Get] one picture of that rock under the descent stage;...

speaker: Bean
text: Will do.

speaker: Conrad
text: ...[then] grab the Hand Tool Carrier and head for the solar wind and grab a picture of that. In the meantime, I'll lope off to the ALSEP and check the SIDE. I'll meet you at Point 1 at Head Crater.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger; we copy.

speaker: Gibson
text: And, Al, have you gotten the readings on the contrast charts?

speaker: Bean
text: Not yet; and I plan to do that real quick.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Conrad
text: Houston, Pete's on his way to the ALSEP.

speaker: Gibson
text: [Making a mis-identification] Roger, Al; we copy. And at 30 minutes into the EVA, you're pretty close to the nominal time line.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay.

speaker: Conrad
text: Very good. [Pause] Can the guy with the seismometer hear me running?

speaker: Bean
text: [Garbled; possibly something about a camera setting] [Long Pause] Okay.

speaker: Gibson
text: Pete, we're watching you down here on the seismic data. Looks as though you're really thundering right by it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah, I ground to a halt there to switch to intermediate cooling . I notice that it is obviously a little bit hotter out here with the higher Sun angle right now. [Pause] Okay. I'm approaching the infamous SIDE.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. And we were able to copy [that is, sense] your rest and now that you're moving again [on the seismometer].

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. [Pause] All right, Houston. The [CCIG] status is...Oops, I'm going to get dust in it. The cover is off, and it's pointed up at the sky at about a 60-degree angle.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. Do not touch it right now, Pete. Which way is that pointing, relative to east-west?

speaker: Conrad
text: It is pointed down-Sun [that is, west].

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. [Pause] Pete, no need to change the configuration; let's press on. [Pause] We copy that you've stopped on the seismic.

speaker: Conrad
text: Yeah. Where's me handy-dandy LMP?

speaker: Bean
text: He's contrast charting.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, okay. Meet you at the Head Crater, pal.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, boy, is that...I want that rock. That is a dandy extra grapefruit-size-type goody. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: [I need to] find a crater with a shadow in it first. There's one. [Pause] Okay, Houston, I'm approaching a crater now and I'm going to put the contrast chart in it. One [photo taken with the chart placed] on each side [of the contact between sunlight and shadow]. One on the sunny side, one on the shadow side. [Garbled]

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. [Pause]

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. There's the one on the sunny side.

speaker: Gordon
text: Go ahead, Houston.

speaker: Conrad
text: Man, have I got the grapefruit rock of all grapefruit rocks! That's got to come home in the spacecraft; it'll never fit in the rock box. [Pause] Okay, Houston, I'll tell you what I'm going to do. I'm going to wind up at the right place at Head Crater; and, while I'm waiting for Al, I'll roll a boulder for you.

speaker: Gibson
text: Clipper, would you give us the configuration of your high-gain system?

speaker: Gordon
text: Roger. It's in Reacq now - Servo Electronics, and Secondary.

speaker: Schmitt
text: Sounds good, Pete.

speaker: Bean
text: I'm now looking at the contrast...[Pause] [Sub vocal, taking a picture of the contrast chart on a level surface] Five [feet focus] and one [picture].

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. Copy Reacq. And say last.[Pause.]

speaker: Schmitt
text: Pete, Houston. Can you give us a mark when you roll? Over

speaker: Conrad
text: That crater is...[Answering Houston] Yeah, I sure will. Head Crater is, by golly, a rather steep crater; a lot steeper than it looks from out the LM. It's...

speaker: Gibson
text: Dick, we copy that you have - in the Reacq position and say your second comment?

speaker: Gordon
text: It's Reacq, Narrow Beam width, Servo Electronics in Secondary.

speaker: Bean
text: Houston?

speaker: Schmitt
text: Yeah, go.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger. Copy Narrow and Secondary. Dick, we have a map update for you when you're ready to copy.

speaker: Bean
text: I'm looking at the contrast chart in the Sun and I can see all the different shades. Okay, now I've taken a photo of it; now I'll look at the one in the shadow. In the shadow, I can see...Well, it kind of depends on how close I am. If I'm within about 3 feet of it or 4 feet of it, I can see all six shades. I'll take a picture here, then I'll back up.

speaker: Gibson
text: If you'd like, we'll hold up until we can get you off relay.

speaker: Gordon
text: You're going to have to if you want me to hear.

speaker: Conrad
text: Let me ask you a question, Houston. How big a rock?

speaker: Schmitt
text: Pete, Houston. I presume whatever's a convenient size for you. We'll check that out though.

speaker: Conrad
text: [chuckles] How about a grapefruit-size rock? That's what I'm holding in my hand and these other rocks that I was talking to you about are pretty well buried, and they're pretty large. I don't think I could get one of them going.

speaker: Bean
text: Houston?

speaker: Schmitt
text: [To Pete] Roger. We copy. Grapefruit-size or any size is fine.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Al, are you standing still?

speaker: Bean
text: Yeah, I'll stand still; go ahead.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. I'm standing still. Houston, on my mark, gonna roll it.

speaker: Conrad
text: Mark. It's starting down. Hit, hit, hit, hit. [About one second intervals] Now it's just rolling. Roll, roll, roll, still rolling.

speaker: Schmitt
text: Roger, Pete. We've got some jiggles...

speaker: Conrad
text: Roll, roll, roll.

speaker: Schmitt
text: ...that I can see here. We'll get a reading on it for you.

speaker: Conrad
text: Still rolling. Still rolling. Very slowly, still rolling. And it's stopped...

speaker: Conrad
text: Mark. Stop. [Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, Houston, I'm looking at the contrast chart in the shadow and, as I mentioned, at 3 feet I can see all six. If I back up maybe to 10 feet, as long as I stand here a moment and adapt my eyes, I can see all six, also. Now, the thing that seems to have the biggest effect on it is how low the Sun is. The Sun is high now and so I don't have to squint my eyes particularly looking in that direction [of the Sun]. Yesterday, looking into the same crater - even though it wouldn't be any darker in there - because the Sun was there, I would never be able to adapt. Right now, I can see all six marks, and I've taken the photographs. Going to go out and do solar wind now.

speaker: Schmitt
text: Roger, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: I can't see a lot of difference in visibility here as on Earth, really. You adapt just as well. The only major difference I've noticed is the fact that when you're out here on this area, if you look cross-Sun, the Moon appears one color; if you look down-Sun, it's another; if you look up-Sun, it's another. But looking into shadows or anything else like that, it's pretty much the same as [looking into shadow] on Earth.

speaker: Gibson
text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. We've dropped the relay; we have a map update, Rev 26, when you're ready to copy.

speaker: Gordon
text: Okay, go ahead.

speaker: Gibson
text: Copy that, Al.

speaker: Schmitt
text: Copy that, Al.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, I'll take some pictures here of the solar wind for you. [Long Pause] It doesn't look as pronounced wrapped around the pole now that I get out here, Houston. It looks pretty much like yesterday. I guess it was sort of an optical illusion from inside the spacecraft. [Pause] I took a couple of pictures of it, but I don't think there's anything unusual going on there.

speaker: Gordon
text: Clipper copies.

speaker: Schmitt
text: Roger, Al. And, Pete, if it's convenient and you can find another rock there and give her a heave, Experiments sure would like to see another one.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay, I was setting up my rock hole and all that good things for the polarizing light. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Say, I was looking at a rock that has small crystals in it. One of them is shining very, very bright green, like ginger-ale-bottle green. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Al, are you on your way?

speaker: Bean
text: That's affirm; I'm now making sure that everything is in the Hand Tool Carrier here.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: I'm mounting them pretty firmly. Hey, Houston. As I was working around the Hand Tool Carrier a moment ago, the canvas bag [the big sample bag in the middle of the HTC] came loose. It took me about 2 minutes to put it back together again; it came off the metal sides. And it looks like those clips that hold it on are going to be completely inadequate and I expect that we're going to have some trouble with it all day today. Maybe you ought to think about fixing it before the next time [that is, before Apollo 13].

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. We copy that. Do you think that once you put a little weight in it, she'll hold better?

speaker: Bean
text: I don't know; they don't seem to have a lot of friction on the sides there, and that bag just floats around. It needs to be more firmly attached some way.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause]

speaker: Conrad
text: Al?

speaker: Bean
text: Yes, sir.

speaker: Conrad
text: Where are you?

speaker: Bean
text: I'm just leaving the LM.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay.

speaker: Bean
text: Boy, this Hand Tool Carrier is light and nice compared to carrying it around on Earth. [Pause] I think we might be able to just slip it right down inside the Surveyor crater with us. Piece of cake. Okay. I see you over there; I'm on the way.

speaker: Conrad
text: Oh, don't tell me, you ding-a-ling camera. Man! [Long Pause]

speaker: Bean
text: I can see everything from fine-grain basalt - as I come running across the area here - to a few fair[ly] coarse-grain ones. I see some sort of light reddish-grey colored rock that I would call...[Pause] I don't know really what I would call it. It looks almost like a granite, but of course it probably isn't, but it has the same sort of texture. The individual components - constituents - aren't as big crystals [as in a typical granite] but it still has that same [reddish] appearance.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. We copy that. And, Pete, can we give you any help with that camera?

speaker: Conrad
text: [With a confident, pure Pete Conrad tone] I got it going, just fine.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Conrad
text: I'm taking the polarized pictures right now. [Pause] Al, when you get up to me, if you'll just stop up-Sun at 15 feet and take that shot of what I'm shooting f/11:15, two pictures: one before, one after.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, let me take something out of this crater hole, Pete. It's sort of unusual; it's got a lot of those little droplets on it, those blebs. But the fragments in this crater look different from the others. [I'll] take a couple of quick pictures, then I'll be right with you.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. It's all working out just fine.

speaker: Bean
text: [I'll] give them a stereopair of this [that is, a pair of pictures of the same scene, taken a couple of feet apart]. [Pause] Good. Let me use the tongs here, and I'll pick it up. [Pause] It's right exactly...This is a very small crater, Houston, probably about 3 feet in diameter and looks like it was made [by a] not very fast moving or energetic or heavy projectile. Yet, right in the middle of the hole is some of these glass-covered rock fragments. And, on some of the other rocks that seemed to be rested in the hole - I'm putting them all in a sample bag - [reading and reporting the label number] 1 - here, I mean...Some of the others don't have any coating on them at all. I'm picking them up with the tongs, but I can't tell how strong they are but they don't seem to hold together too well; they seem kind of weak. There you go. Now, I'll head over where Pete is.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Al. We copy that. If you're going to document that, try to get some of the material around the glass as well as the glass itself [to see whether or not the glass and the non-melted portions of the projectile were once part of the same rock or whether the glass represents a coating].

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. I want to...I'll just get this as a bonus. I want to get over here and start working with Pete as a team, here.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger.

speaker: Bean
text: Just didn't want to have to try to remember where that was.

speaker: Conrad
text: You're going to get a big surprise when you look into this Head Crater, Al. It's a heck of a lot deeper than it looked.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. [Pause] Here's a nice white, small crater with a white rim on it [at R.05/13.18 on the Planimetric map ]. About a 5-foot diameter one. [Change in voice volume] I've been concentrating, Houston, as I came walking over here to Head Crater, to see if there were any possible changes in either texture, slope, color or anything you can think of - or anything that I could think of - that would say to me that I was walking on a different surface than I was when I started. And haven't seen a thing yet; it all looks the same. It all looks like it's covered with this...

speaker: Conrad
text: Slow up.

speaker: Bean
text: ...black rock.

speaker: Conrad
text: Don't - don't - don't kick dust in the middle of my polarized picture area, here.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. I'll stop right here.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay. Put the tool carrier down and get your up-Sun [means down-Sun] pictures. You see where my footsteps are, that rock that's half buried and the two rocks that I've turned over in my footsteps?

speaker: Bean
text: Yeah.

speaker: Conrad
text: Okay; it's 15 feet, f/11. Two shots. Now, you're not going to get the before, unfortunately.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay. How about right...[Would you] rather have my shadow here or over there?

speaker: Conrad
text: No, that's the pile, right there. See where I turned over the two rocks alongside the great big rock, where my foot tracks are?

speaker: Bean
text: Oh yeah, way down there at the end.

speaker: Conrad
text: No, right here. [Pause] I'll walk over to it.

speaker: Bean

speaker: Bean
text: You'd better believe it.

speaker: Conrad
text: I can't see.

speaker: Bean
text: Okay, pull up a little bit and I'll bring it in.

text: The Sun's shining right in my eyes.

speaker: Bean
text: That's it.

speaker: Conrad

text: Beautiful job; just throw the LEC out. Okay, Houston. ETB is in with the [LM TV] camera and all the film, and so forth and so on.

speaker: Gibson
text: Roger, Pete. Copy you got the ETB in with the TV camera, close-up stereo [film magazine], and the [70 mm] film packs.

speaker: Bean
